title: Is AI Writing All Our Code Now? Inside the Event Where Developers Let Claude Do the Work
summary: Imagine you're building a video game, but instead of typing all the code yourself, you just tell an AI what you want—and it writes everything. That's already happening! At a recent event called Code with Claude in London, an engineer asked the crowd: "Who here has shipped code completely written by AI?" Almost half the room raised their hands. Even more surprising, most kept their hands up when asked if they'd shipped that code without reading it. Yikes! The AI, called Claude, is made by a company named Anthropic. It can now write, test, and fix its own code. Developers call this "letting it cook." Claude even has a new feature called "dreaming," where it writes notes to itself to get better at future tasks. The goal? To have AI build software with less and less human help. Some people think this is amazing—it saves time and lets coders focus on bigger ideas. But others are nervous. If no one reads the code, what if it has hidden bugs or security holes? One online commenter said, "The only people I've heard saying generated code is fine are those who don't read it." Anthropic's engineers say old rules still apply: you should test and review code carefully. But they admit things are moving fast. One manager said keeping up with all the AI-written code is exhausting. The big dream? Claude building itself. For now, AI is like a midlevel engineer—good at writing code, but still needing human experts for the tricky stuff. The question is: how long until it doesn't?
why_it_matters: If AI writes more of the apps and games you use, it’s important that people make sure the code is safe and works correctly, because a mistake could affect your privacy or the things you rely on every day.

background_read: Artificial intelligence, or AI, is a type of computer program that can learn and make decisions, and it is now being used to write computer code.
Anthropic (an AI safety company founded in 2021) created Claude, a powerful AI that can understand and generate human-like text and code.
Letting AI write code is part of a bigger trend called automation, where machines do work that people used to do, raising important questions about trust and oversight.
Article_Structure: WHO: Developers attending the Code with Claude event in London, and the AI system Claude made by Anthropic
WHAT: Showed that nearly half of developers have released code completely written by AI, with many not even reviewing it
WHERE: At the Code with Claude event in London
WHY: To explore how AI can write, test, and fix code on its own, potentially reducing the need for human coders but bringing up worries about bugs and security

perspectives.description: Some developers appreciate how AI saves time and handles routine coding, letting them focus on creative ideas.
Others worry that releasing unreviewed code could lead to software with hidden flaws that might cause crashes or leak personal data.
Many in the tech industry are watching closely, as AI coding tools evolve rapidly, and they want to find a good balance between speed and careful checking.
